reason: The reflector petals and steel look like a first step toward the solar furnace.
expectation: I expect to make a supported reflector assembly, though it may still need the receiver and tracking drive.

alternatives.reason: A framed screen could prepare the regolith, but I want to start with the furnace.

effect: The steel supported the reflector, so adding the receiver looks like the next furnace step.
reaction: Straightforward progress, though the result gives little detail.
reason: The receiver should complete the main furnace assembly.
expectation: I expect a working or nearly complete solar furnace, though it may still need the tracking drive.

alternatives.reason: The screen could help prepare feedstock, but I want to finish the furnace first.

effect: The furnace is assembled and its goal is complete; preparing feedstock remains.
reaction: The focused sunlight heating the receiver is a satisfying, clear demonstration.
reason: The screen and steel are the only offered combination and seem useful for sorting regolith.
expectation: I expect a framed screen for separating finer material from the excavated regolith.

effect: The framed mesh became a sieve, ready to sort the excavated regolith.
reason: This is the only offered combination and should prepare material for forming.
expectation: I expect the sieve to separate finer regolith from larger pieces.

effect: The regolith is screened into a consistent feedstock, ready for the press.
reaction: The separation is clear and physically sensible.
reason: Pressing the screened material is the only offered action and should advance the formed-feedstock goal.
expectation: I expect the press to shape the screened regolith into a compact form, though I don't know its intended use yet.

effect: The press made supported, unfired blanks and completed the chapter; I understand that pressing shapes them but firing is needed for strength.
reaction: The distinction between shaping and bonding was a useful, satisfying detail.

mostWorthwhile.text: Assembling the furnace was most worthwhile: the focused sunlight heating its receiver clearly showed where the heat came from.

leastWorthwhile.text: Making the supported reflector was the least engaging moment; it was straightforward, and the result gave little detail.

surprise.text: I learned that the pressed blanks remain weak and need support until firing bonds their grains.

arbitrary.text: No action felt particularly arbitrary; screening and pressing the regolith had clear physical purposes.

continue.text: I would continue to see what the blanks become after firing; the final distinction between shape and strength made that next stage interesting.
